captions.detailed: This 3D-printable object is a rectangular socket box designed to house banana plug connectors. It features a hollow rectangular main body with open top and bottom faces, framed by walls of uniform thickness. One of the long vertical side walls is punctured by three evenly spaced circular holes aligned horizontally, providing access points for wire connections or plugs.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric banana plug socket block in OpenSCAD with a customizable number of holes, hole diameter, wall thickness, and overall height. The design should consist of a hollowed-out rectangular block with the specified number of circular connector holes evenly spaced along one of its long side faces.
captions.factory: The code starts with parametric variables for the number of holes, their diameter, wall thickness, and total height. An outer cube is created to form the main block, and an inner, slightly smaller cube is subtracted using the difference() operator to hollow it out, leaving a bottom and side walls. A for-loop iterates through the specified number of holes, subtracting cylinder primitives from one of the long side walls of the block. Finally, the entire assembly is rotated 90 degrees around the X-axis so that the hollowed-out opening faces upwards.
